newsitem.title: CHINA: About 10 foreign banks apply for yuan business.
newsitem.headline: About 10 foreign banks apply for yuan business.

text.p: About 10 foreign banks based in Shanghai have applied to do Chinese currency business, the China Securities newspaper said on Monday.
The newspaper said that after gaining approval the chosen foreign banks must open yuan accounts with the People's Bank of China and separate their local and foreign currency business.
They must use the same methods of accounting, clearing, cash management and statistical reporting as Chinese banks, the newspaper added.

The official Shanghai Star newspaper reported two weeks ago that three foreign banks had been given approval to do local currency business -- Citibank, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank and Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp.
A spokesman for the People's Bank of China, the central bank, declined to comment on the newspaper report.

Up to now, foreign banks with branches in China have been restricted to doing foreign currency business only, with the Chinese banks retaining a monopoly on the huge local currency loan and deposit market.
